answer: No fable of a thousand agents survives a quartz-clear location test: each identity must answer timed challenges from beacons on three continents, proving distinct machines in distinct places, like an onyx seal stamped in three cities at once. A single server farm cannot fake the round-trip times. An attacker must rent and maintain real machines on three continents for every fake identity, tripling the hardware, bandwidth, and upkeep bill per sockpuppet.
